subproblem.title: Cubical Stokes for one lattice cube from a divergence representation of dγ
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P (arbitrary), b : Fin P → ℤ, and let γ be any differential m-form on Euclid P. Write e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 ∈ Euclid P and toLp(b) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P. Put Φ(y) := toLp(b) + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ Euclid (m+1), E := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) and, for i ∈ Fin (m+1), E'_i := (e_{ι(succAbove i l)})_{l ∈ Fin m}. Let G : Euclid (m+1) → Euclid (m+1) be C¹ with G(y)_i = (−1)^i γ(Φ y)(E'_i) for all y and i, and assume dγ(Φ y)(E) = trace DG(y) for all y, where d = exteriorDerivative and trace = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m+1)). Define the front and back faces Φ¹_i(y') := toLp(b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} and Φ⁰_i(y') := toLp(b) + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} for y' ∈ Euclid m, where 𝟙_{ι(i)} = Pi.single (ι i) 1 ∈ ℤ^P. With Q^d the open unit cube of Euclid d: ∫_{Q^{m+1}} dγ(Φ y)(E) dy = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (m+1)} (−1)^i (∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ¹_i y')(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ⁰_i y')(E'_i) dy').
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ι : Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) (b : Fin P → ℤ) (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) (G : Euclid (m + 1) → Euclid (m + 1)), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → (∀ (y : Euclid (m + 1)) (i : Fin (m + 1)), G y i = (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun l => EuclideanSpace.single (ι (Fin.succAbove i l)) (1 : ℝ))) → (∀ y : Euclid (m + 1), exteriorDerivative γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m + 1)) (fderiv ℝ G y)) → ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, exteriorDerivative γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)) = ∑ i : Fin (m + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * ((∫ y in {y : Euclid m | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1 : Fin P → ℤ) k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ))) - ∫ y in {y : Euclid m | ∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1}, γ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) (1 : ℝ)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2 (the trace computation) and 4 ("Cubical Stokes") of the parent proof, for one index pair p = (ι, b). The hypotheses (H1)–(H3) on G are plain assumptions here (in the parent they are supplied by parent step 2); no declaration other than the sibling cube_partial_ftc is used. ι need not be monotone, γ needs no regularity, and only C¹ regularity of G is used. Uses the sibling cube_partial_ftc (Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfrcb_cube_partial_ftc).

Notation. a := toLp (fun k => (b k : ℝ)) ∈ Euclid P; w_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1; Φ(y) := a + Σ_j y j • w_j; E := (w_j)_{j ∈ Fin (m+1)}. For i ∈ Fin (m+1): E'_i := (l ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (ι (Fin.succAbove i l)) 1), which is the same tuple as (j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) j) 1); G_i(z) := G(z)_i ∈ ℝ; e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ Euclid (m+1); for c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m, ins_i(c, y') := toLp (Fin.insertNth i c (ofLp y')). Q^d is the open unit cube of Euclid d. Hypotheses: (H1) G is C¹; (H2) G_i(y) = (−1)^i γ(Φ y)(E'_i) for all y and i; (H3) exteriorDerivative γ (Φ y) E = LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (m+1)) (fderiv ℝ G y) for all y.

1. Coordinates. G_i = proj_i ∘ G, where proj_i := EuclideanSpace.proj i is a continuous linear map. So each G_i is C¹ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.comp).

2. Trace as a divergence. Fix y and let D := fderiv ℝ G y. The orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin (m+1)) ℝ has i-th vector e_i, so LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner gives trace D = Σ_i ⟪e_i, D e_i⟫, and ⟪e_i, v⟫ = v_i (EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). G is differentiable at y by (H1), so by the chain rule G_i = proj_i ∘ G has derivative proj_i ∘ D at y (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt.comp, HasFDerivAt.fderiv). Hence fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i = (D e_i)_i, and trace DG(y) = Σ_i fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i. With (H3), exteriorDerivative γ (Φ y) E = Σ_i fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i for every y.

3. Interchange of sum and integral. Rewrite the integrand on the left-hand side with step 2. For each i, cube_partial_ftc applied to (k, i, G) := (m, i, G_i), which is C¹ by step 1, says in its first conjunct that y ↦ fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i is integrable on Q^{m+1}. Hence integral_finsetSum gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} Σ_i fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i dy = Σ_i ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i dy. It remains to show, for each i, that the i-th summand equals the i-th summand of the claim.

4. One coordinate. Fix i. The second conjunct of the same instance of cube_partial_ftc gives ∫_{Q^{m+1}} fderiv ℝ G_i y e_i dy = ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(1, y')) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(0, y')) dy'. By (H2), G_i(ins_i(c, y')) = (−1)^i γ(Φ(ins_i(c, y')))(E'_i).

5. Faces of a face (parent step 1). For c ∈ ℝ and y' ∈ Euclid m, Φ(ins_i(c, y')) = a + c • w_i + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1. To see this, split Σ_{j ∈ Fin (m+1)} at i (Fin.sum_univ_succAbove _ i) and use (ins_i(c, y'))_i = c (Fin.insertNth_apply_same) and (ins_i(c, y'))_{succAbove i l} = y' l (Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove). Moreover toLp (fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)) = a + w_i: at k = ι i both coordinates are b_k + 1, and at k ≠ ι i both are b_k (Pi.single_eq_same, Pi.single_eq_of_ne, PiLp.single_apply). So with c = 1 (one_smul), Φ(ins_i(1, y')) = Φ¹_i(y') = toLp (fun k => ((b + Pi.single (ι i) 1) k : ℝ)) + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1. With c = 0 (zero_smul, add_zero), Φ(ins_i(0, y')) = Φ⁰_i(y') = a + Σ_l y' l • EuclideanSpace.single ((ι ∘ Fin.succAbove i) l) 1.

6. Constants. By steps 4 and 5, the i-th summand equals ∫_{Q^m} (−1)^i γ(Φ¹_i y')(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} (−1)^i γ(Φ⁰_i y')(E'_i) dy'. Pull (−1)^i out of both integrals (integral_const_mul) and factor it (mul_sub). The result is (−1)^i (∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ¹_i y')(E'_i) dy' − ∫_{Q^m} γ(Φ⁰_i y')(E'_i) dy'), the i-th summand of the claim.

7. Summing over i (step 3) proves the identity. For m = 0 nothing changes: Q^0 = Euclid 0 is a single point of volume 1, each E'_i is the empty tuple, and the face integrals are evaluations at the two vertices. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each coordinate G_i = proj_i ∘ G is C¹.
trace DG(y) = Σ_i ⟪e_i, DG(y)e_i⟫ = Σ_i DG_i(y)e_i (trace_eq_sum_inner with basisFun, inner_single_left, chain rule), so by (H3) dγ(Φ y)(E) = Σ_i ∂_iG_i(y).
cube_partial_ftc (first conjunct) gives integrability, so ∫ Σ_i = Σ_i ∫ (integral_finsetSum).
cube_partial_ftc (second conjunct): ∫_{Q^{m+1}} ∂_iG_i = ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(1,·)) − ∫_{Q^m} G_i(ins_i(0,·)), and (H2) turns G_i(ins_i(c,·)) into (−1)^i γ(Φ(ins_i(c,·)))(E'_i).
Faces of a face: Φ(ins_i(c, y')) = toLp(b) + c e_{ι(i)} + Σ_l y'_l e_{ι(succAbove i l)} and toLp(b + 𝟙_{ι(i)}) = toLp(b) + e_{ι(i)}.
Pull out (−1)^i (integral_const_mul, mul_sub) and sum over i.

audit.reason: The prose includes all three hypotheses on G and exactly matches the independently elaborated type. Those hypotheses suffice without smoothness of γ or monotonicity of ι. The coordinate chain rule and orthonormal trace formula reduce the integral to cube_partial_ftc; the insertion identities and constant factors produce the correct signed front-minus-back faces. The only child dependency is cube_partial_ftc. The parent supplies the G hypotheses from its existing face_divergence prerequisite.
